description: We are a group of enthusiasts of applied mathematics and artificial intelligence.
summary:
ASTRO-CARE is an interactive, offline-capable astronaut health monitoring web application built with HTML/JavaScript and backed by a Python data pipeline analyzing real NASA datasets.
Addressing the Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts challenge, our tool integrates environmental radiation monitoring with human biomedical indicators across three operational levels: continuous dosimetry, non-invasive urine screening, and capillary blood/metabolic checks. Using 251,734 real ISS radiation measurements from NASA RadLab (DosTel1, revealing peaks up to 622.8 μGy/h) alongside astronaut clinical panels from NASA OSDR—Blood Count (OSD-569), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (OSD-575), and Urine Immune markers (OSD-656)—we extracted sex-specific clinical reference ranges and identified high-impact spaceflight biomarkers such as absolute lymphocytes, glucose, VCAM1, and CCL23.
Astronauts can input daily metrics or test mission scenarios, visualize real NASA trends, and receive instant Green/Yellow/Red risk alerts with actionable countermeasures aligned with NASA-STD-3001 and Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines. This empowers crew autonomy and early radiobiological protection when Earth communication is delayed.
details:
What it does: ASTRO-CARE is a browser-based clinical decision-support dashboard designed for astronauts operating under communication delays with Earth. It evaluates radiation exposure alongside immune, hematological, and metabolic health in a single lightweight interface that runs 100% offline.

How it works:

  1. Data Analysis Pipeline (Python / Google Colab): We processed 251,734 ISS radiation readings (rad.csv from DosTel1) and three SpaceX Inspiration4 biomedical datasets (LSDS-7 CBC, LSDS-8 CMP, LSDS-64 Urine multiplex). Our script computed pre-flight vs. post-flight (R+1) shifts, extracted male/female clinical reference ranges (RANGE_MIN–RANGE_MAX), identified orbital radiation spikes (up to 622.811 μGy/h), and exported a compact JSON/JS dataset (datos_nasa_completo.js).
    • Level 1 (Passive Dosimetry): Tracks instantaneous dose rate (μGy/h) and cumulative career effective dose (mSv) against the NASA-STD-3001 600 mSv limit.
    • Level 2 (Non-invasive Urine Screening): Monitors inflammatory/endothelial proteins (VCAM1, CCL23, TNFSF8) without needles in microgravity.
    • Level 3 (Capillary Blood & Metabolic Confirmation): Evaluates radiosensitive lymphocytes, WBC, hemoglobin, glucose (mg/dL), and calcium using sex-specific NASA limits.
  2. Combined Risk Engine & HRP Guidance: Outputs a Green/Yellow/Red status and actionable countermeasures (shielding protocols, ALARA, hydration, and Flight Surgeon alerts).

Benefits & Impact: Reduces unnecessary blood draws in microgravity, gives crew members clear visual feedback on space radiation and physiological stress, and works reliably without continuous internet connectivity.

To use our application, download the two files: indexv2.html and datos_nasa_completo.js. Simply run indexv2.html, and it will open in Google Chrome—no internet connection required.
dataRefs: NASA RadLab (ISS DosTel1): 251,734 real absorbed dose rate measurements (μGy/h) aboard the International Space Station, used to characterize baseline exposure, orbital radiation spikes (up to 622.811 μGy/h), and daily exposure trends.

NASA OSDR – OSD-569 (LSDS-7_Complete_Blood_Count_CBC): Real astronaut hematology panels (23 analytes, preflight vs. postflight R+1), used to extract sex-specific clinical ranges and track radiosensitive immune cells (e.g., Absolute Lymphocytes).
NASA OSDR – OSD-575 (LSDS-8_Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel_CMP): Real astronaut metabolic panels (19 analytes, including Glucose and Calcium), used for metabolic and bone-health thresholds.

NASA OSDR – OSD-656 (LSDS-64_Multiplex_urine.immune.AlamarPanel): Real astronaut urine immune/inflammatory proteomics, used to identify the top 10 post-flight altered proteins (VCAM1, CCL23, TNFSF8) for non-invasive screening.
